summary: Technical risk assessment for the BRC event-pump + durable memory refactor. The proposal removes the structural seam (model volunteering to re-enter blocking wait) by lifting the wait to the wrapper, with memory carried in a per-role brc-memory.md and continuity sequenced from server-side next-action queries. Most risks are MEDIUM and manageable with explicit mitigations the planner must encode. Two risks are HIGH and gate plan-phase consensus: (R1) the existing state-store and health-monitor durability does NOT meet the cq-3 hard requirement that the no-progress safety budget and parked HITL decisions survive SDLC-host failure, and (R2) the Qwen-route provider-cache TTL ceiling against realistic ~10-13 min BRC idles is unmeasured. R1 must be addressed by an explicit durability extension in the plan (synchronous flush on HITL writes + state-store-backed safety budget); R2 must be addressed by WS0 spike instrumentation of a ~15 min idle on the Qwen route before any v1 cutover. Verdict on the plan-as-framed (Option B + the cq-1/2/3/4 HITL resolutions): ACK with the two HIGH risks tracked and mitigations enforced; the architect / task_planner producers will be reviewed against the same lens when they propose.
verdict_rationale: The recommended Option B is the only option that removes the structural seam rather than narrowing it. The WS7 measurement work has already de-risked the cache concern on both routes for short/medium idles. The remaining HIGH risks (cq-3 durability gap, Qwen TTL ceiling) are addressable in the plan and the issue body explicitly leaves them as 'resolve during implementation against spike data'. NACK conditions for architect / task_planner are tracked separately under blocking_concerns once those producers propose.

risks.title: Existing state-store + health-monitor do NOT meet cq-3's host-death-recoverable hard requirement
evidence: orchestrator/state_store.py:719-740 — pipeline state is written atomically to disk via temp-file+rename, then committed to git, then pushed to remote via an async best-effort daemon thread (lines 805, 890-928).

If a save_pipeline() returns successfully and the host crashes before the async push fires, the state is stranded on emptyDir-backed pod-local disk. orchestrator-deployment.yaml:188-191 — both /home and .egg-state are emptyDir volumes, so a pod restart wipes them.
orchestrator/state_store.py:304-305 — _restore_from_remote() finds nothing on remote and silently creates a fresh orphan branch, losing the decision state.

orchestrator/health_monitor.py:82-103, 133-144, 286-810 — _agents, _last_heartbeat, AgentState.last_progress, progress_escalated are entirely in-memory. No persistence. A pod restart resets all wall-clock progress anchors to zero; a pipeline that had been silently progressing for 550s before a crash will have 0s elapsed when the monitor re-initializes.

HITL cq-3 resolution explicitly states: 'this no-progress safety budget is now the ONLY safety net, so it must be robust to SDLC-host failure. The parked HITL decision AND the safety-budget / no-progress state must be persisted DURABLY SERVER-SIDE.'
risks.primitive_existence_check: FAIL — the operator's requirement assumes a primitive (durable server-side state) that exists in the form 'best-effort async git push' rather than 'synchronous flush before returning'. The current shape is a known stochastic-loss surface.
risks.trust_boundary_check: BOUNDARY VIOLATION — the orchestrator returns success to the agent before the durable write has actually crossed the host boundary onto remote storage.
mitigations: Plan MUST introduce a synchronous-flush variant of save_pipeline() for HITL-decision writes and safety-budget writes. Either (a) synchronously await the git push and surface failure to the caller, or (b) write to a remote-first store (orchestrator Redis with AOF / Postgres / git-server via blocking HTTP) before acking the mutation.

Plan MUST extend the health monitor to checkpoint last_progress + progress_escalated to the same durable store on every heartbeat-threshold-crossing transition (not on every heartbeat — that would thrash). Reload on startup as part of startup_reconciliation.py.

Plan MUST add a startup-reconciliation path that replays the safety budget from the durable store rather than reinitialising to zero (the BRC consensus-tracker reconstruction at cli.py:292-387 is the existing precedent).
Tester / coder verification gate: end-to-end test that kills the orchestrator pod mid-HITL-resolution and confirms the resolved decision survives the restart.
risks.rollback: If durability work proves too large for this issue's scope, the plan should fall back to keeping the old capped-restart wrapper available (which contradicts cq-4 — operator override required) OR explicitly defer cq-3's durable-safety-budget requirement to a follow-up and surface the resulting reduced-durability posture as a HITL gate before v1 cutover. The current plan-phase risk register flags either fallback path as an operator escalation.
risks.owner: coder (durability work) + reviewer_plan (gate enforcement) + operator (if rollback path taken)

risks.title: Qwen-route provider-cache TTL ceiling vs realistic ~10-13 min BRC idles is unmeasured
risks.impact: MEDIUM (cost) / HIGH (if widespread cache misses force a redesign post-cutover)
risks.likelihood: MEDIUM — TTL is known ≥5.5 min, unknown vs ~15 min; observed BRC idles reach 10-13 min on real pipelines.
evidence: Issue WS7 follow-up comment: 'TTL ceiling unmeasured. Observed BRC idles reached ~10-13 min (a producer composing). So the only open question: does the Qwen provider cache survive a ~15-min idle?'

config/litellm/patch_litellm_cache.py:104-152 — egg only unstrips OpenRouter's native Qwen cache_control header; it adds no custom caching. OpenRouter / Alibaba TTL is provider-side, undocumented in this codebase.

HITL cq-2 resolution: 'WS0 must instrument the actual per-event cold-read / cache-creation cost on the Qwen route across a realistic worst-case BRC idle (specifically a reviewer parked while a producer addresses a NACK and re-proposes — observed ~7-8 min in practice).'

config/litellm/cost_callback.py:1-60 — per-call usage is logged to stdout; the host-side ~/.local/state/clm/cost-*.json is NOT how in-pod agents observe their own cache. The WS0 instrumentation must source Qwen numbers from the litellm callback, not from the Agent SDK result (which is all-zero on the Qwen route).
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS structurally — the cost callback exists and emits per-call cache numbers. But the WS0 work needs to wire those into an aggregated 'per-event cold-read cost across a synthetic 15-min idle' measurement that does not exist today.
risks.trust_boundary_check: External provider — egg cannot guarantee the TTL ceiling and has no recourse if OpenRouter/Alibaba changes it. The plan must treat this as an external-dependency risk and instrument continuously rather than assume.
mitigations: WS0 spike MUST include a ~15 min idle measurement on the Qwen route, sourced from the cost_callback stdout stream (not Agent SDK usage.* which is zero on this route). Per HITL cq-2: 'ONLY if that measured cold-read waste proves material should a BOUNDED keep-warm be added, and then: Qwen-route only, active only during idles approaching the TTL, with a capped total number of refreshes, and SUPPRESSED during HITL / awaiting-human waits.'

If the TTL ceiling proves <15 min: keep-warm cadence < measured TTL, Qwen-route only, with a cap on total refreshes and explicit suppression during AWAITING_HUMAN states. The keep-warm must NOT run on the Anthropic route (1h TTL makes it unnecessary).
Instrument provider cache_read ratio in steady-state ops (not just spike) so a TTL change post-cutover is detected before it costs serial pipeline runs.
Per HITL feedback Q1: no hard caps; instrument-and-report. The operator will judge go/no-go from the reported numbers — the plan must surface those numbers, not gate them automatically.
risks.rollback: If WS0 measures the Qwen TTL ceiling as materially worse than the Anthropic route AND keep-warm cost projection is unacceptable to the operator, the plan ships v1 on the Anthropic route only and the Qwen route stays on the new event-pump without keep-warm (accepting the higher cold-read cost — operator decision under cq-2 explicitly allows this since Qwen tokens are cheap).
risks.owner: spike-author (WS0 measurement) + coder (keep-warm if needed) + operator (go/no-go judgment)

risks.title: Wait-loop cursor at /tmp/egg-wait-cursor-* is wiped on pod restart; wrapper-side wait must handle stale cursors
risks.impact: MEDIUM — stale cursor causes either duplicate event processing or missed events depending on server-side since_id handling
risks.likelihood: LOW per pipeline (pod restart is rare under normal ops) / HIGH across the deployment lifetime
evidence: sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:1377-1512 — cursor file path is /tmp/egg-wait-cursor-{pipeline_id}-{role}-{md5_hash} (line 1426). /tmp is ephemeral in Kubernetes.
Lines 1461-1465 document that stale cursors are deleted when the server signals since_id_stale: true; recovery depends on the orchestrator's server-side since_id resolution (#2464).
Wrapper takeover of the wait does not change the cursor mechanism's ephemerality — same /tmp path, same wipe-on-restart behaviour.
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS — the server-side since_id_stale signal exists per #2464.
risks.trust_boundary_check: PASS — cursor is correctly scoped per-(pipeline, role, filter-hash).
mitigations: Plan MUST confirm the new wrapper-driven wait continues to honour the since_id_stale server signal (i.e. the egg-orch message wait-loop CLI's existing behaviour must not be circumvented by a bespoke wrapper-side wait that bypasses the CLI).
If the wrapper builds its own wait loop instead of invoking the existing egg-orch message wait-loop CLI, it MUST reimplement the cursor file write/read + stale-signal handling.
Tester verification: simulate pod restart mid-wait; confirm event delivery resumes correctly (either replay-from-start or server-side cursor recovery).
risks.rollback: Wrapper's wait can fall back to a durable cursor location under .egg-state/ (gateway-allowed) instead of /tmp.

risks.title: Gateway credential / session expiry during long event-pump idles
risks.impact: HIGH — agent re-spawn fails silently with stale bearer tokens; gateway treats the role as session-expired
risks.likelihood: LOW for short idles / MEDIUM for long HITL-awaiting waits (which the operator explicitly noted can last hours, per HITL cq-2)
evidence: Existing consensus_wrapper risk note (from code exploration): 'If gateway credentials expire during a 15-minute restart wait, agents re-spawned on restart will fail with stale bearer tokens.'
sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py — wait-loop heartbeat at 60s interval drives gateway-session keep-alive (#2451). Default gateway idle window is 60 minutes.

Wrapper takeover: the wait-loop's daemon thread (_start_wait_loop_heartbeat, lines 234-264) is currently inside the in-pod agent process. If wrapper takes ownership of the wait, the wrapper must also take ownership of the keep-alive POST with the same slice_id resolution semantics.
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS — heartbeat endpoint, slice_id resolution, container-id reconstruction (egg-agent-{pid}-{slice}-{role}) all exist.
risks.trust_boundary_check: BOUNDARY-PRESERVING — wrapper runs in same pod, has same env vars (EGG_AGENT_ROLE, EGG_PIPELINE_ID, EGG_SLICE_ID, EGG_GATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN), can emit heartbeats on the agent's behalf.
mitigations: Plan MUST migrate the 60s heartbeat from the in-agent message_wait_loop daemon thread to the wrapper. Wrapper resolves slice_id at entry (existing resolve_slice_id helper) and POSTs WAITING_FOR_EVENT heartbeats during waits, WORKING heartbeats during agent invocations.

Plan MUST handle the AWAITING_HUMAN case (idles up to hours per cq-2): keep-alive must continue during HITL waits, OR the gateway session must be specifically marked as 'human-bound' and not subject to the 60-min idle expiry.
Tester verification: artificially induce a 75-min idle; confirm gateway session survives, agent re-spawn succeeds, no 401s from gateway.
risks.rollback: If wrapper-side heartbeat proves fragile, retain the in-agent message_wait_loop heartbeat as a fallback by keeping that primitive callable but moving its triggering to a wrapper-spawned background helper.

risks.title: Memory file shape (append-only vs distill) is load-bearing for both cost AND correctness; no committed decision criterion yet
risks.impact: MEDIUM — wrong choice either inflates per-event cost (distilled bursts memory-cache) or constrains agent attention (append-only sea-of-context per agent-mode-design.md)
risks.likelihood: HIGH — Open Decision #1 in the issue body is not yet resolved
evidence: Issue body 'Open decisions (resolve during implementation, several against spike data)' item 1: 'Memory location/schema/shape — append-only (cache-friendly, grows, needs compaction) vs rewrite/distill (bounded, busts memory-cache each event).'

Refine-phase analysis line 360-367: 'The planner should additionally evaluate against the orient, don't constrain axis from docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md: an unbounded append-only memory eventually starts constraining what the per-event agent can attend to (sea-of-context), while a distilled memory keeps small summaries that orient as the target shape.'

Refine-phase analysis line 168-177: memory-delta MUST be metadata not content; the agent fetches diffs on demand. This constrains both shape options — the memory file holds prior verdicts, not file contents.

HITL feedback Q2 (operator): 'Ephemeral coordination state — brc-memory.md can be cleaned up with the pod; the orchestrator message history is the durable reconstruction backstop. HARD CAVEAT: this is acceptable ONLY because recovery must NOT depend on the ephemeral memory file surviving.'
risks.primitive_existence_check: MIXED — .egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/ already exists in every role's allowlist per shared/egg_restrictions/patterns.py; the memory file shape itself is the open question.
risks.trust_boundary_check: PASS — within role's write boundary. Cross-role reads (a producer reading another producer's memory) should be confirmed against the existing allowlist before relying on it for the dual-role-reviewer flow.
mitigations: Plan MUST commit to a memory shape with explicit rationale evaluated against BOTH axes: (a) cache cost (does the shape burst the per-event prefix?) AND (b) orient-don't-constrain (does the shape constrain the agent's attention as it grows?). The refine-phase analysis flags this — the plan should not leave it open.

Plan MUST encode the cq-2-Q2 hard caveat: any plan slice that depends on brc-memory.md surviving a pod restart for correctness escalates back as a NACK condition. Memory file is coordination state; orchestrator message history is the recovery backstop.

Plan MUST action-scaffold the memory writes off brc_ack / brc_nack handlers (which already carry reason + files_reviewed) rather than free-form journaling — mitigates curation reliability (per refine-phase Option B 'Cons' / 'Mitigated by').

Tester verification: agent invocation with prior memory + new event produces verdict consistent with what an agent without prior memory would produce given the same event + delta — i.e., memory orients, does not bias.
Spike verification: measure per-event cache_read ratio under both shapes on the Qwen route (sensitive case); pick the one that meets both axes.
risks.rollback: Start with distilled / bounded shape (per orient-don't-constrain); if WS0 measurement shows it busts cache materially on Qwen, add an append-only tail with compaction at a threshold. Distilled is the default if the decision must be made before spike data lands.

risks.title: Adding CLI commands without retiring MCP tools breaks the existing drift-test invariant
risks.impact: MEDIUM — CI break that blocks merge; not a correctness regression
risks.likelihood: HIGH — the existing test asserts gap-set equality and will FAIL when new CLI verbs are added
evidence: tests/tools/test_mcp_cli_drift.py:264-290 — maintains an explicit expected_gaps set; test_cli_less_tools_are_documented_gaps() at line 243 asserts actual_gaps == expected_gaps at line 286.
tests/sandbox/egg_agent_tools/test_server.py:110 — hard-coded TOOL_LIST count of 31; will FAIL if new MCP tools added.
HITL cq-1 resolution: 'Do NOT delete the existing MCP tools in this issue — just guarantee CLI availability for the event-pump's needs.'
New CLI verbs required by WS3 (and used by the wrapper / per-event agent): brc get-state, brc list-blocking, phase get-context, brc resolve-obligation (iter-2), brc read-peer-artifact (iter-2).
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS — handlers (brc.brc_get_state at handlers/brc.py:679, etc.) all accept dict[str, Any] kwargs cleanly serializable as CLI args.
risks.trust_boundary_check: PASS — adding a CLI is parity with existing handler invocation; no new write boundary.
mitigations: Plan MUST budget for updating test_mcp_cli_drift.py:264 expected_gaps and test_server.py:110 TOOL_LIST count as part of WS3 / WS8-net-new task scope.

Plan SHOULD update test_mcp_cli_drift.py to assert 'no MCP tool exists without a CLI peer' (which is what the test is really driving toward) rather than maintaining a hand-tended gap list — the cq-1-resolved direction is 'reduce the gap, eventually delete the MCP surface'.

Plan MUST flag that prose-bearing CLIs (consensus propose/ack/nack) are explicitly DEFERRED per cq-1 and the new CLI commands (read-only queries) do not trigger the #2741 prose-corruption risk — but the pattern-consistency rule (stdin/file for prose) still applies if any new CLI accepts prose arguments.
risks.rollback: Tests can be temporarily marked xfail if the underlying invariant change scope blows the issue's diff budget; coder then opens a follow-up to land the gap-set / count update.
risks.owner: coder (CLI commands + test updates) + reviewer_plan (test-budget enforcement)

risks.title: Prior-fix preservation: cursor threading (#2323), pre-confirm-wait (#2064/#2482), gap-race (#1995), heartbeat (#2036), gateway keep-alive (#2451), open-NACK aggregation (#2142), conditional-ACK + stale-version re-review (#2482), producer-allowlist scope (#2725)
risks.impact: HIGH per individual regression (one of these is the root cause of every prior production incident in the lineage)
risks.likelihood: MEDIUM — the wrapper takeover restructures the surface that hosts each of these, and the BRC preamble (_build_brc_preamble at orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:12348) is being prompt-collapsed
risks.severity: MEDIUM (each is mitigated by existing test coverage if it's exercised; risk is in the prompt-collapse losing the operator instructions that named the fix)
evidence: Refine-phase analysis line 181-185 explicitly calls out these as prior-fix preservation requirements.

Existing tests: cursor-related in sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:1377-1512 (md5 cursor key); pre-confirm-wait rejection at handler level (HTTP 400 on CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED in pre-confirm wait); gap-race in sandbox/egg_agent_tools/handlers/message.py (since_id threading); heartbeat at message.py:175-264; gateway keep-alive at orchestrator/routes/heartbeats (egg-agent container_id reconstruction); open-NACK aggregation at orchestrator BRC propose handler (HTTP 409 inline details); conditional-ACK + stale-version at orchestrator/routes/consensus.

WS6 prompt collapse target (_build_brc_preamble) currently encodes some of these as inline instructions to the agent. If they're collapsed into a lean event-handler contract that omits the instruction, the agent may regress behaviour that the orchestrator still enforces — most failure modes become 400/409 retries, which is loud but wasteful.
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS — each fix has both code + tests today.
risks.trust_boundary_check: MIXED — some fixes (e.g. #2142 open-NACK aggregation) are orchestrator-side enforced and survive prompt collapse; others (e.g. #2323 cursor threading) live in the CLI and are preserved only if the wrapper uses the CLI rather than rolling its own.
mitigations: Plan MUST inventory each prior fix in the WS1 wrapper migration plan and identify whether it survives by (a) being orchestrator-enforced (safe), (b) being in the CLI the wrapper invokes (safe if wrapper uses CLI), or (c) being inline prompt instruction (REQUIRES preserving the instruction in the lean event-handler contract).

Tester verification gate: the existing tests for each of these fixes (#2323 cursor tests, #2064/#2482 pre-confirm rejection tests, #1995 gap-race tests, #2036 heartbeat tests, #2451 gateway keep-alive tests, #2142 aggregation tests, #2725 allowlist tests) MUST still pass under the new wrapper.
Plan MUST include a regression test gate for each fix; reviewer_plan blocks consensus if any are removed without explicit operator approval.
risks.rollback: If a fix proves load-bearing in a way that doesn't survive the lean event-handler contract, restore the relevant prompt instruction explicitly. The mission is reducing the BRC preamble, not eliminating it.

risks.title: cq-4 deletes the old capped-restart wrapper entirely — no flag — invalidating any in-flight or stuck pipeline at cutover
risks.impact: HIGH — pipelines mid-restart-loop at cutover are dropped into the new event-pump with no recovery instructions; could orphan in-flight work
evidence: HITL cq-4 resolution: 'Delete the old capped-restart wrapper path entirely — do NOT retain it behind a flag.'

Refine-phase analysis line 178-180 (Constraints): 'Backwards compatibility for in-flight pipelines. The capped-restart wrapper path must remain reachable behind a flag until the new path is validated, so cohorts that started on the old path can finish on it.' — DIRECTLY CONTRADICTED by cq-4 resolution.
orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py:38 (MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS = 3) and the surrounding restart-loop logic are the deletion target.
concurrent_executor.py:37 and routes/pipelines.py:2792 are the consumers of build_consensus_wrapped_command — both must be migrated atomically.
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS — both consumers are identified; atomic migration is achievable in one PR.
risks.trust_boundary_check: PASS — same wrapper boundary, just different control flow inside it.
mitigations: Plan MUST include a cutover procedure (drain in-flight pipelines before the deployment containing the deletion, OR gate the new path on a per-pipeline 'event_pump_enabled' flag set at pipeline creation so cohorts opt in cleanly).

Plan MUST update routes/pipelines.py:2792 (which currently calls build_consensus_wrapped_command inside a phase-restart flow) to be a no-op or removed if phase-restart concept survives the safety-budget redesign.
Tester verification: simulate a pipeline mid-restart-loop at the moment of cutover; confirm graceful migration or graceful FAIL (not silent orphaning).
Note: refine-phase constraint 'capped-restart must remain reachable behind a flag' is REPLACED by the cq-4 operator override; the plan should not re-introduce a flag without an operator decision.
risks.rollback: If cutover orphans pipelines, redeploy the old path is the only option (revert + rebuild). This is one-way without a flag, so the cutover plan must be exceptionally well-rehearsed.

risks.title: Server-side 'consensus next-action --role R' endpoint underspecified; risks reproducing orchestrator state-machine logic in the per-event agent
risks.impact: MEDIUM — if next-action is incomplete, the agent re-derives lifecycle state from raw consensus status, which is fragile and was the prior failure mode
evidence: Issue body WS3: 'Reuse egg-orch consensus status --json if sufficient, else a thin consensus next-action --role R.'
Refine-phase analysis line 327-330 — primitive 'egg-orch consensus status --json' is identified but lifecycle decoding is left to the agent.

Lifecycle complexity that the endpoint must cover: producer step (orient → work → propose → respond-to-reviews → confirm → stay-alive), reviewer step (prepare → poll → sync → review → ack/nack → confirm → stay-alive), dual-role agents (producer-step first per #2749), open-NACK aggregation barrier #2142 (HTTP 409 inline details for 2+ reviewer NACKs), conditional-ACK with pre-merge-condition (#1998), stale-version rejection #2482, resolve_obligation #2338.

Per the dual-role banner in this role's task description: 'Execute the lifecycles in this strict order' — encoding this rule in a server endpoint moves the rule out of the prompt where it's currently lived-by-instruction.
risks.primitive_existence_check: PARTIAL — consensus status exists; next-action does not. Building it is WS3-net-new and must precede WS1's dependence on it.
mitigations: Plan MUST decompose WS3 into: (a) define the next-action enum (PROPOSE, RESPOND_TO_REVIEW, REVIEW_PROPOSAL, CONFIRM, STAY_ALIVE, RESOLVE_OBLIGATION, IMPASSE-ESCALATE) and (b) implement the endpoint that maps {role, current consensus state, slice scope, dual-role mode} → next-action. Both before WS1 depends on it.
Plan MUST cover the dual-role producer-first ordering (#2749) explicitly in the endpoint, since this is currently a prompt-only rule.
Plan MUST cover the open-NACK aggregation barrier (#2142) in the endpoint's return: a producer with 2+ pending NACKs should see RESPOND_TO_REVIEW with all-NACKs inline, not just the most recent one.
Tester verification: contract tests for the endpoint covering each lifecycle step + each known prior-fix scenario.
risks.rollback: If WS3 scope blows up, fall back to consensus status + agent-side lifecycle decoding, retaining the BRC preamble's lifecycle instructions until WS3 lands. This effectively makes WS6 (prompt collapse) partially-blocked on WS3 completion.

risks.title: Per-event subprocess + Python interpreter startup latency accumulates across rapid event arrivals
risks.impact: LOW per event (~100ms-1s); MEDIUM if event-storms (e.g. multiple concurrent ACKs converging) cause wall-clock inflation
risks.likelihood: MEDIUM — BRC events are often clustered (e.g. all reviewers ACK within seconds of each other)
evidence: shared/egg_agent/command.py:11-46 — each build_agent_command() call constructs a fresh subprocess; consensus_wrapper.py:178-180 executes it freshly per event.
shared/egg_agent/__main__.py:24-64 — run_agent() invoked fresh per process spawn; no cross-event state accumulation.

Issue body Open Decision 6: 'WS8 latency trade — CLI = subprocess + interpreter spawn per call vs in-process MCP dispatch. Likely negligible for a handful of calls per event, but measure per-event wall-clock; if it bites, a persistent egg-orch daemon/socket or batched calls are fallbacks.'
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS — subprocess spawn is the current pattern; no new primitive.
mitigations: WS0 spike MUST measure per-event wall-clock for the SDK entry point invocation (not just cache cost) across a representative BRC cycle.

If latency proves material, the plan SHOULD consider event coalescing in the wrapper (e.g. drain the queue and pass all pending events in one invocation), with the constraint that the per-event agent's verdicts on each must remain independent.
The CLI commands added in WS3 (get-state, list-blocking, get-context) are CLI = subprocess + interpreter — if WS3 calls accumulate, consider a persistent CLI daemon socket as a Phase 2 optimisation.
risks.rollback: If latency is unacceptable on the Qwen route specifically, the in-process MCP server stays (cq-1 already preserves this) and only the new CLI commands need to be wired for the wrapper itself, not the agent.

risks.title: Risk that implementation regresses the refine-phase fix and re-introduces 'claude -p' / 'claude --print' as the per-event invocation
risks.impact: HIGH — would re-introduce the EGG100-linted anti-pattern that the refine phase explicitly corrected
risks.likelihood: LOW — the refine analysis is explicit, but the issue body itself still contains 'SDK-native one-shot claude -p' phrasing in the design block
evidence: Refine analysis line 41-58: 'Primitive correction relative to the issue body. The issue text refers to SDK-native one-shot claude -p. That phrasing is incorrect for egg: claude --print is an EGG100-linted anti-pattern (docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md:90-104).'

docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md:90-104 documents the lint rule; sandbox/egg_lib/gha_exec.py:101 is the only documented exception (one-shot GHA exec), whose docstring at lines 88-92 explicitly steers long-running tool-using agents toward build_agent_command().
orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py:748-759 already uses 'python3 -m egg_agent' with the explicit comment 'Uses the Agent SDK entry point instead of the claude CLI.'
Risk: a coder reading the issue body's 'claude -p' phrasing as authoritative could re-introduce the anti-pattern; the refine analysis is the authoritative correction.
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS — build_agent_command() and python3 -m egg_agent exist and are the correct primitive.
mitigations: Plan MUST cite docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md:90-104 in the wrapper-migration task description and require coder to use build_agent_command() / python3 -m egg_agent (NOT claude --print).

Plan MUST budget the EGG100 lint to remain enforced; any new claude --print call would be caught by lint and is acceptable ONLY in the existing gha_exec.py exception (which is not the consensus wrapper).
Reviewer_plan verification: read the WS1 wrapper migration task; confirm the primitive named is python3 -m egg_agent, not claude --print or claude -p.
risks.rollback: If the coder regresses, the EGG100 lint catches it pre-merge.
risks.owner: coder (primitive choice) + reviewer_plan (lint enforcement) + reviewer_code (lint enforcement in implement)

risks.title: Risk of baking large diffs / file-contents into per-event prompts instead of metadata-only delta
risks.impact: MEDIUM — re-introduces the 'baking in large diffs' anti-pattern from agent-mode-design.md; inflates per-event cost and constrains agent attention
risks.likelihood: MEDIUM — the easiest implementation of 'delta-only re-analysis' is to inline the diff; the correct implementation is to surface only metadata
evidence: Refine-phase analysis line 168-177 (Constraints): 'Memory-delta is metadata, not content. Delta-only re-analysis means the agent receives the prior assessment summary + a metadata delta (changed file paths, commit SHAs, version markers, NACK reasons), NOT an inlined diff blob or file-contents snapshot baked into the per-event prompt.'
docs/guides/agent-mode-design.md (referenced in refine analysis) — 'baking in large diffs' is named anti-pattern.
Risk surfaces in WS5 (delta-scoped re-analysis): the simplest implementation is changed_artifacts-style metadata; the wrong implementation is a pre-fetched diff blob.
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS — git tools available in-pod; agent can fetch its own diffs.

risks.title: SSE event-pump silent-failure mode (consensus_wrapper.py:423-501) has no fallback alert if curl times out without consensus.reached
risks.impact: MEDIUM — silent stuck pipeline; operator only learns when downstream timeouts fire (which may not exist)
risks.likelihood: MEDIUM — SSE endpoint failures are infrequent but happen (network blips, orchestrator restarts)
evidence: Existing code at orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py:423-501 — SSE primary with curl --max-time, fall through to egg-orch message wait, fall through to sleep. The new event-pump generalises this pattern.
Risk note from code exploration: 'If curl times out without consensus.reached event, falls through with no observability. The new always-on event-pump must add explicit heartbeats during long waits.'
risks.primitive_existence_check: PASS — wrapper heartbeat is being added under WS4 anyway.
mitigations: Plan MUST ensure the wrapper emits WAITING_FOR_EVENT heartbeats during long waits (the WS4 liveness migration covers this).

Plan SHOULD add an OVERSEER_ALERT trigger if the wrapper sees N consecutive curl-timeout-without-event cycles (e.g. 5x the expected event interval), so the operator gets visibility on stuck waits before the no-progress safety budget fires.
Tester verification: kill the SSE endpoint mid-wait, confirm the wrapper emits heartbeats and eventually alerts.
risks.rollback: Heartbeats are already in scope (WS4); the extra OVERSEER_ALERT trigger is an optional addition.

rollback_plan_summary: Rollback granularity is per-workstream. WS0 (spike) is informational — no rollback. WS1 (wrapper) deletes the old capped-restart path per cq-4 with no flag — rollback is git revert + redeploy, which orphans any in-flight pipelines started post-deletion. WS2 (memory) is additive — rollback by deleting the brc-memory.md files (none of which are authoritative per cq-2-Q2). WS3 (next-action) is additive — rollback by reverting the endpoint + CLI. WS4 (liveness migration) is the one area where rollback is hardest — if the wrapper-side heartbeat breaks gateway sessions in production, the fix is to re-enable the in-agent daemon thread, which requires re-deploying the old message_wait_loop primitive. WS5/WS6 (delta + prompt collapse) are agent-side and rollback is by reverting the BRC preamble. WS7 (cache, if keep-warm needed) is Qwen-route-only, ops-time-gated, suppressed during AWAITING_HUMAN — rollback by disabling the loop. WS8 (net-new CLI commands only — no MCP deletion in this issue per cq-1) is additive, rollback by removing the CLI verbs. Most workstreams are individually revert-safe; WS1 + WS4 require coordinated rollback if cutover goes wrong, and the cq-4 no-flag deletion makes WS1 rollback the highest-effort path.
